name: France
standard: RGAA 4.1.2 (French transposition of EN 301 549 / WCAG 2.1 AA); RGAA 5 in drafting, expected end 2026

laws.cite: Loi n° 2005-102 du 11 février 2005, art. 47 and 47-1
laws.summary: Public sector bodies and large companies must make online public communication services accessible, with Arcom as the regulator.
Sets RGAA, the accessibility statement, the multi-year plan and the mandatory homepage mention.
Created art. 47-1 giving Arcom control and sanction powers, and transposed the EAA.

applies_to: Public legal entities; private bodies with a delegated public service mission; private companies with over EUR 250m average annual French turnover over 3 years (for large companies Arcom only controls the disclosure obligations).
exceptions: Disproportionate burden (dérogation pour charge disproportionnée), which must be listed in the statement
requires: Accessibility statement (déclaration d'accessibilité) stating conformity: total, partial (at least 50% of criteria) or none
Homepage mention 'Accessibilité : totalement / partiellement / non conforme'
Multi-year accessibility plan (schéma pluriannuel) plus annual action plans
Accessible feedback mechanism (email or form) and a notice of the right to contact the Défenseur des droits
Update the statement on substantial change, 3 years after publication, or 18 months after a new RGAA methodology
mobile: explicit — the statement rules cover mobile apps (published on the website or at download); RGAA applies to apps.
procurement: Not captured in sources opened; RGAA is used as the contractual reference in French public tenders.
enforcement: Arcom (art. 47-1): sworn agents record the breach, then a public formal notice to comply. Fines up to EUR 50,000 for accessibility failures and up to EUR 25,000 for statement, plan or mention failures, scaled by severity and duration.
notes: The brief said 'RGAA 4.1'; the current version is 4.1.2 (2023-04-18). The Légifrance URLs for the loi, décret and ordonnance are standard JORF identifiers but were not opened here, so verify them. France extended the duty beyond WAD to large companies.
